Breast Cancer DNA-Methylation — Results Overview

What we did, what we found, and where every result lives — in plain English.
TCGA-BRCA (888 samples: 791 tumor / 97 normal) + GSE66695 (120 samples) · Illumina HM450 array · ~485,000 CpG sites

1. What we did (in one paragraph)

DNA methylation is a chemical “on/off” layer on top of the DNA that controls which genes are switched on. We measured it at ~485,000 positions across the genome in 888 breast samples, compared tumor vs. normal tissue, and identified the exact sites and genes the tumor has switched off (by adding methylation to a gene’s on-switch / promoter → silencing) or on (by removing it → activation). We then validated the result two independent ways and mapped the changes onto longevity/anti-aging genes.

3. Data visualizations

Volcano plot. Every dot is a CpG site: how big the tumor-vs-normal difference is (left–right) vs. how confident we are (bottom–top). The many dots high up and far out = strong, reliable differences.
PCA plot. Each dot is a sample. Tumor and normal samples fall into clearly separated groups — visual proof the methylation signal cleanly distinguishes the two.
Heatmap. Top marker sites (rows) across samples (columns); red/blue shows high/low methylation. Tumor and normal form distinct blocks.

4. Did we trust it? Two independent checks

Validation 1 — internal (leakage audit + nested cross-validation). Tested whether the near-perfect result was real or the model “cheating.” After a leakage-proof re-check, accuracy stayed at AUC ≈ 0.996. The signal is real.
Validation 2 — external cohort (GSE66695). Tested whether the markers hold in a completely separate patient group from a different lab. They did (hyper markers +0.28, hypo markers −0.21 tumor-vs-normal). It replicates.

8. Longevity genes in healthy tissue — the site atlas

For 1,953 longevity/anti-aging genes across 40 categories (telomere, stem-cell, mitochondrial, FGF, etc.) we built an atlas of 43,609 individual CpG sites, each with its exact coordinate and its methylation state in healthy tissue (green = unmethylated/active, red = methylated/silenced). It is delivered as an interactive Excel dashboard.

Honest note on “pathways.” When we tested whether whole longevity pathways are enriched, none survived the field-standard statistical correction — the initial hits were an artifact of the array design (bigger genes carry more probes and look enriched by chance). So our confident findings are at the site level (specific genes and coordinates, like FGF2), not the broad pathway level. This is the honest, stronger position.

10. Bottom line

  • Breast tumors carry a strong, real, reproducible methylation signature (validated internally and in an independent cohort).
  • We predicted ~99,000 gene-silencing and ~61,000 gene-activation events, each mapped to an exact site.
  • The FGF2 promoter is unmethylated/active in healthy tissue and becomes silenced in tumor — a clean, cross-validated, site-level finding.
  • Broad pathway-level longevity claims did not survive rigorous correction — reported honestly as a negative result.
